planting.note: Plant divisions in early fall or spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Dixie Chick is a 1999 Plant Delights (Tony Avent) introduction bred from 'Masquerade' x 'Invincible'.

directions: Dixie Chick forms a small, vigorous mound of narrow, glossy, dark green leaves marked with an irregular creamy-white center streak inherited from its streaked parent 'Masquerade', while its other parent, the tough green 'Invincible', contributes a sturdy root system and fast bulking habit. Pale lavender flowers appear on short scapes above the foliage in summer. Its mini-to-small mature size and vigor make it a reliable, easy-to-grow choice for the front of a shaded border, edging, or rock garden.

planting.note: Plant divisions in early fall or spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Lakeside Dragonfly was registered in 1997 by Mary Chastain of Lakeside Acres Nursery in Tennessee.

directions: Lakeside Dragonfly produces broad, lance-shaped leaves that emerge blue-green with soft creamy-yellow margins in spring, then shift through the season to a shinier medium green with crisper, pure white margins, giving the clump a changing, painterly look as the leaves mature. Pale lavender flowers appear on tall scapes in late summer, followed by viable seed. It is a fast-growing, dense-spreading cultivar well suited to a mixed shade border or container where its shifting variegation can be appreciated up close.

common_name: Winter Snow Hosta (Giant White-Margined Sport of Sum and Substance)

planting.note: Plant divisions in early fall or spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Winter Snow is a variegated sport of the giant 'Sum and Substance'.

directions: Winter Snow bears enormous, shiny, heart-shaped leaves with a vibrant chartreuse-to-light-green center and a wide, creamy-white margin, a dramatic variegated counterpart to its all-gold parent 'Sum and Substance'. Pale lavender flowers rise on tall scapes in mid to late summer well above the foliage mound. Because it is sized like other giant hostas, give it ample room and several years to reach its full, imposing scale.

common_name: Tiny Tears Hosta (Classic Miniature Green Hosta)

planting.note: Plant divisions in early fall or spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Tiny Tears was registered in 1977 by Robert Savory of Savory's Gardens in Minnesota as a seedling of Hosta venusta.

directions: Tiny Tears forms a dense, rapidly spreading mound of small, tear-shaped dark green leaves, one of the earliest true-miniature hostas widely grown and still a benchmark for the category decades after its introduction. Medium purple flowers appear from late June into July, followed by viable seed. Its fast growth and tidy, diminutive habit suit edging, troughs, and the front of a shaded path where larger hostas would overwhelm the scale.

planting.note: Plant divisions in early fall or spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Shiny Penny was bred by Bob Solberg of Green Hill Farm from 'Lemon Lime' x 'Shining Tot' and registered in 1997.

directions: Shiny Penny opens with thick, heart-shaped new foliage in bright golden yellow that mellows to light green as the leaves age, with a top surface and an especially glossy underside that catches the light differently from most hosta leaves. Lavender flowers appear on short scapes in July. It is a fast-growing miniature well suited to containers, rock gardens, and the front of a shaded bed where its shifting gold-to-green color is easy to appreciate.

common_name: Bitsy Gold Hosta (Narrow-Leaved Miniature Gold Hosta)

planting.note: Plant divisions in early fall or spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Bitsy Gold was registered in 1985 by Robert Savory of Savory's Gardens, a cross involving Hosta longissima and a gold seedling.

directions: Bitsy Gold forms a low, tidy mound of narrow, slightly wavy, elliptic gold leaves, the yellow-leaved counterpart to the green-leaved 'Bitsy Green', and the two look especially good planted together alternating along a path edge. Lavender flowers appear on short scapes from late July into August. Its small mature size and slow, steady growth make it a good fit for troughs and the front of a small-scale shaded planting.

planting.note: Plant divisions in early fall or spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in full to partial shade; Cat's Eye is a Japanese-bred Hosta venusta hybrid and is considered a slower, more exacting collector's miniature.

directions: Cat's Eye forms a tiny, rounded mound of small, dark green leaves, each centered with a wide, creamy-white blaze that narrows the overall look to a bright eye-like highlight against the darker margin. Lavender flowers appear on short scapes in midsummer. It is considered a more challenging grower than most Mouse Ears-type miniatures and performs best given close attention to consistent moisture and protection from pushier neighbors, making it best suited to troughs or a dedicated miniature-hosta bed rather than a general border.

common_name: Hush Puppy Hosta (Ruffled Cream-Edged Small Hosta)

planting.note: Plant divisions in early fall or spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Hush Puppy is a Plant Delights Nursery (Tony Avent) introduction.

directions: Hush Puppy produces small, twisted, perky leaves edged in cream over a green center, the twisting giving the clump a softly ruffled texture that sets it apart from flatter-leaved small hostas. Lavender to purple flowers appear on scapes above the foliage in summer. It forms a tidy, symmetrical little mound well suited to edging, troughs, and the front of a shaded bed.

planting.note: Plant divisions in early fall or spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; El Capitan was registered in 1987 by Wm. and Eleanor Lachman of Massachusetts as a seedling of 'Beatrice'.

directions: El Capitan forms a very large mound of heart-shaped, heavily puckered sage-green leaves outlined with an irregular bright gold margin, a pairing noted at its introduction for unusually heavy leaf substance at this scale. Medium lavender flowers appear on tall scapes in late July, followed by viable seed. Give it ample room and several growing seasons to reach its full imposing size, and avoid dividing it more often than necessary since large hostas rebuild slowly after disturbance.

common_name: Dolce Mocha Mint Heuchera (Silver-Leaved Coral Bells with Dark Veins)

planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Dolce Mocha Mint is part of Terra Nova Nurseries' Dolce series of heat-tolerant coral bells.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; sharp drainage matters as much as consistent moisture, since heuchera crowns rot in soggy sites. Dolce Mocha Mint bears small, rounded, lobed leaves in a silvery-gray tone traced with contrasting dark green veins, forming a dense basal mound. Slender spires of tiny coral-red flowers rise well above the foliage in late spring into early summer. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to keep the mound tidy and vigorous.

common_name: Dolce Creme de Menthe Heuchera (Mint-Green Coral Bells with Silvery Sheen)

planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Dolce Creme de Menthe is part of Terra Nova Nurseries' Dolce series of heat-tolerant coral bells.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, with reliable drainage to prevent crown rot. Dolce Creme de Menthe produces lobed, rounded leaves in mint green overlaid with a silvery sheen and etched with deep green veins, the leaf undersides a contrasting dark rose, and the whole mound can take on a reddish blush as temperatures cool in fall. Tiny creamy-pink flowers appear in spires above the foliage in late spring into early summer. Keep soil evenly moist through summer heat and divide every few years in spring once the clump becomes crowded.

common_name: Carnival Watermelon Heuchera (Frosted Peach-Bronze Coral Bells)

planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Carnival Watermelon is a Heuchera villosa hybrid introduced by Terra Nova Nurseries in 2014, bred for heat tolerance and uniform habit.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; the villosa parentage behind the Carnival series gives it noticeably better heat and humidity tolerance than older heuchera cultivars. Carnival Watermelon forms a neat, uniform mound of lobed leaves ranging from greenish-bronze to pinkish-peach with a soft frosted overlay that shifts tone through the season. Delicate creamy-white flower spikes rise above the foliage in early to midsummer, lifting the overall height to about 18 inches. Divide crowded clumps in spring every few years to maintain a tidy mound.

common_name: Carnival Limeade Heuchera (Bright Lime-Green Coral Bells with Dark Veins)

planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Carnival Limeade is a Heuchera villosa hybrid bred for heat tolerance and uniform habit.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; good drainage combined with even moisture keeps the villosa-type Carnival series performing well through summer heat. Carnival Limeade bears bright lime-green, lobed leaves with a soft frosted overlay and contrasting dark veins, forming a compact, well-proportioned mound. Small flower spikes rise above the foliage in early summer, bringing the overall height to around 16 inches. Divide congested clumps in spring every few years to refresh the planting.

common_name: Carnival Plum Crazy Heuchera (Deep Purple Coral Bells with Silver Overlay)

planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Carnival Plum Crazy is a Heuchera villosa hybrid introduced by Terra Nova Nurseries in 2014, bred for heat tolerance and uniform habit.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; the villosa background behind the Carnival series helps the foliage hold its color through hot, humid summers better than many older coral bells. Carnival Plum Crazy produces deep purple, lobed leaves with a frosty silver overlay on top and contrasting purple undersides, forming a dense, neat mound. Fine flower spikes appear above the foliage in early summer, raising the overall height to roughly 18 inches. Divide crowded clumps every few years in spring to keep the planting vigorous.

common_name: Carnival Candy Apple Heuchera (Crimson-to-Brick-Red Coral Bells)

planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Carnival Candy Apple is a Heuchera villosa hybrid introduced by Terra Nova Nurseries in 2015, bred for heat tolerance and uniform habit, with best foliage color in some shade.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade, since partial shade brings out the richest foliage color in this cultivar. Carnival Candy Apple opens with crinkled, lobed leaves in deep crimson that mature to brick red overlaid with coppery-bronze and silver highlights, forming a tidy, uniform mound typical of the villosa-type Carnival series. Delicate creamy-white flower spikes appear above the foliage in early to midsummer, raising the overall height to about 18 inches. Divide congested clumps every few years in spring to maintain vigor and shape.
